title: An XML API whose parser still resolves external entities turns any file the service can read into an out-of-band disclosure channel
index_line: T-0064 · FILE_READ · an unauthenticated XML API with external entities on by default: DOCTYPE + SYSTEM entity reads service files, OOB parameter entities exfiltrate them · java · corroborated
invariant_violated: The XML parser behind an API assumed nobody hostile would hand it a document, so DTD processing and external-entity resolution stayed enabled by default; the platform also assumed its own configuration files, certificates and keys would only ever be read by itself.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated client submits an XML message whose document carries a DOCTYPE with external entities to the provisioning interface (OCI-P)
the platform's XML parser processes the DTD as part of the document instead of rejecting it (entity resolution allowed by default)
an entity's SYSTEM identifier points at a server-side file; resolving it reads that file with the service account's privileges
blind variant: a parameter entity embeds the read bytes into a URL the parser then fetches, moving file contents out-of-band to the attacker

source.http.body.value: an OCI XML message on the management/provisioning service (observed on XSP port 2208) — no session required

guard.none.value: no authentication on the XML interface and no DTD/external-entity restriction in the parser configuration

sink.file.read.value: the entity resolver's file read, keyed by the SYSTEM identifier inside the attacker's DOCTYPE

oracle.channel.value: blind cases exfiltrate through the parser's own fetch of a parameter-entity URL (OOB DNS/HTTP); reflected cases return bytes in the response

preconditions.expr: the XML provisioning interface is reachable without authentication
the XML stack resolves external entities by default (no disallow-doctype-decl / external-entities switch)
the platform release ships the vulnerable parser (BroadWorks R23 line in the observed campaign)

success: a DNS query or HTTP fetch arrives at the attacker host carrying bytes read from a server-side file
response or OOB channel contains data that exists only server-side (system identity keys, SSL credentials)
failure_like: parser rejects the DOCTYPE (DOCTYPE is disallowed / 400 on entity use)
authentication is demanded before any XML parsing
false_positive: the interface answering at all is reachability, not XXE — require the entity read demonstrated via reflected or OOB bytes
parser error text mentioning entities is a lead, not proof; match actual file bytes

hazards: any SOAP/XML-RPC/custom-XML API whose stack still allows DTDs — SOAP is XML, and legacy/telecom/embedded parsers are the residual exposure
the files worth reading are the service's own keys and configs: the observed chain used the platform identity key to impersonate components
blind XXE needs one egress path (the parser's own fetch); reflected XXE works where entity bytes land in an error or echo
detection: the request is one well-formed XML message — nothing looks like an attack until the OOB fetch fires
non_transfers: parsers configured with disallow-doctype-decl, entity limits or a no-network resolver

evidence.target: Cisco BroadWorks XSP OCI XML parser (CVE-2026-20320; exploited in the wild — Operation Snowball entry point)

provenance.author: Cisco PSIRT (cisco-sa-bworks-xxe-uwUd7CEt)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-20320 exists because external entity resolution is allowed by default in the OCI XML parser; an unauthenticated crafted OCI-P message reads sensitive files; CWE-611; CVSS 3.1 7.5 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

provenance.author: MalBear Labs
provenance.corroborates: in-the-wild use of CVE-2026-20320 as the campaign entry point: crafted OCI request to XSP port 2208 recovered the system identity private key and SSL credentials (XSP 23.0.1.1075)
